reviewer: Independent gpt-6.1-sol high reviewer; draft not authored by reviewer
scope: Complete current Part III purpose/content in plan/chapter-plan.yaml and complete 07/08 Markdown and YAML sidecars. Exact scoped native Vale errors judged individually. Earlier foundations/persistence/dynamics passages searched and read where they supply relevant meanings.
baseline: Undergraduate calculus, probability and linear algebra. No electronics course assumed. Expected value, variance, SD and density are assumed.

findings.issue: The new capacitor relation helps, but physical reasoning still depends on current and voltage without giving their physical meanings. Q and V first appear in Q=CV without an explicit symbol mapping; resistance appears before its role is explained. The conductance definition uses linear read regime before saying what linear means here. The earlier neural chapters use mathematical activation/current models but do not supply this electronics bridge.
findings.repair_requirement: Add a compact bridge before the capacitor calculation: current is charge flow per unit time; voltage measures electrical energy difference per unit charge; identify Q as stored separated charge and V as voltage across the capacitor. State that C is treated as fixed in this relation, give the units if retaining the formula, and explain resistance/conductance as the current response to an applied voltage. Replace linear read regime with a direct statement such as at read voltages where current is approximately proportional to voltage. In I=GV identify I and V directly. Keep this to the physical relationships needed later, not a general electronics lesson.
findings.reason_needed: A reader must explain why input current changes stored voltage and why conductance converts input voltage to a weighted current. Treating the names as self-explanatory leaves the central physical mechanism unstated.

findings.issue: Physical phase configuration is a needed specialist meaning: it is not the timing phase used elsewhere. The current definition repeats phase-change without explaining the material change that stores information.
findings.repair_requirement: Explain in a short phrase that programming changes the material atomic arrangement, for example the proportions of ordered/crystalline and disordered/amorphous regions, which changes resistance. Use only the extra terms that help; do not add crystallography detail.
findings.reason_needed: Without this phrase, the reader knows the PCM abbreviation but cannot state what physically persists after power is removed.

additional_truth_check.new_capacitor_definition: Q=CV is correct for the intended fixed, linear capacitance approximation. Separated charge storage and changing charge through net current correctly explain voltage change. No new physical contradiction found; the missing symbol/assumption bridge is recorded in N1.
additional_truth_check.new_conductance_definition: Current/voltage ratio and inverse resistance agree in the stated linear regime. Explain that regime in plain words as required by N1; the definition is not a claim of globally linear PCM behavior.
additional_truth_check.source_meaning: Stage 1 source identities and limits retained. Current wording changes do not turn the illustrative gain/OU models into measured hardware results. No fresh source download was needed.

necessity_judgments.judgment: Retain quotation, its source context, the three different kinds of memory, chapter route and first-pass guidance. They establish purpose and scope; do not edit exact historical wording to satisfy lint.

Retain the weight/state/decoded-value distinction, scoped working memory definition and invented ring example. The example tests whether changing a remembered value requires changing a weight. Neuromorphic is a necessary family name and is defined at first substantial use.

Retain SRAM, analog state, capacitor, conductance, PCM, nonvolatile and device mismatch because each is used to compare a different storage mechanism or error source. Add only the compact physical meanings in N1/N2. The table has a useful job: it relates stored quantity to role and error. A transistor can remain a component reference at this stage; transistor circuit design is not needed to compare discrete feedback with analog voltage.

Retain the event-to-input-to-state-to-event trace, mixed-signal and in-memory terms, and named platform examples. The platform names are grounded in the stated architecture roles. The final statement links storage survival to state updates, a necessary bridge into feedback.

Retain feedback, gain, effective decay time and the gain-sensitivity example. The scalar equation adds a concrete causal calculation. The fold explains the derivation without making it mandatory for first-pass readers.

Retain the discrete/continuous and digital/analog distinctions. Neutral direction, continuous attractor and Brownian increments have earlier teaching in 01b-persistence and 02-memory-dynamics. Pinning is directly defined and needed for the variance-versus-bias interpretation. The OU derivation explains why restoring errors saturate while neutral errors accumulate. Explicit model/source limitations earn their space.

Retain both early demonstrations because they test different memory tasks. Bistability is necessary, directly defined and restricted to the ongoing conditions. Footnote dates/versions and discrete-resolution qualifications prevent unsupported comparisons.
